provider_query: Stack Overflow question page about creating a Python virtual environment
answer:
Relevant Stack Overflow threads on creating a Python virtual environment:

1. **How can I create a virtual environment with Python 3?** — Recommends `python3 -m venv ./path-to-new-venv` (or `.venv`), plus activation and deactivation. Also covers `virtualenv -p python3`.  
   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43069780/how-can-i-create-a-virtual-environment-with-python-3 [[1]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43069780/how-can-i-create-a-virtual-environment-with-python-3)

2. **What is a virtualenv, and why should I use one?** — Explains isolation of packages and shows `python3 -m venv ENV_DIR`, plus older `virtualenv` / `pyvenv` options and activation on Unix and Windows.  
   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41972261/what-is-a-virtualenv-and-why-should-i-use-one [[2]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41972261/what-is-a-virtualenv-and-why-should-i-use-one)

3. **How to create a venv with a different Python version** — Use the desired interpreter (`python3.9 -m venv …`, `py -3.7 -m venv …`) or `virtualenv -p <path>`. Notes `python3.x-venv` packages on Debian/Ubuntu.  
   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/70422866/how-to-create-a-venv-with-a-different-python-version [[3]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/70422866/how-to-create-a-venv-with-a-different-python-version)

4. **python3 -m venv: how to specify Python point release/version?** — Run `venv` via that exact binary (e.g. `python3.6 -m venv whatever`); also discusses `pyenv` workflows.  
   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54700307/python3-m-venv-how-to-specify-python-point-release-version [[4]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54700307/python3-m-venv-how-to-specify-python-point-release-version)

5. **What's the difference between "virtualenv" and "-m venv"?** — `venv` ships with Python 3 (since 3.3); `virtualenv` is a third-party tool with a broader API. Prefer `python -m venv` when possible.  
   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44091886/whats-the-difference-between-virtualenv-and-m-venv-in-creating-python-virt/44091914 [[5]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44091886/whats-the-difference-between-virtualenv-and-m-venv-in-creating-python-virt/44091914)

6. **How to create a virtualenv in python using cmd** — Corrects the module name: `python -m venv venv` (not `virtualenv` as a module name for the stdlib tool).  
   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72700633/how-to-create-a-virtualenv-in-python-using-cmd [[6]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72700633/how-to-create-a-virtualenv-in-python-using-cmd)

7. **Create Virtual Environment using Python Documentation** — Troubleshooting `python3 -m venv` failures, including missing `python3-venv` / `ensurepip` on Debian/Ubuntu.  
   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56339125/create-virtual-environment-using-python-documentation [[7]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56339125/create-virtual-environment-using-python-documentation)

8. **How to create Python Virtual environment within a python script** — Programmatic creation with `virtualenv.create_environment` or `venv.create`.  
   https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57921255/how-to-create-python-virtual-environment-within-a-python-script [[8]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57921255/how-to-create-python-virtual-environment-within-a-python-script)

Related but conda-focused: **How to create a virtual environment in Python using an environment.yaml file?** uses `conda env create -f environment.yml`, not stdlib `venv`.  
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68104229/how-to-create-a-virtual-environment-in-python-using-an-environment-yaml-file [[9]](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68104229/how-to-create-a-virtual-environment-in-python-using-an-environment-yaml-file)

To create a virtual environment, go to your project’s directory and run the following command. This will create a new virtual environment in a local folder named .venv:

```none
python3 -m venv .venv
```

Activate a virtual environment

```none
source .venv/bin/activate
```

To confirm the virtual environment is activated, check the location of your Python interpreter:

```none
which python
```

To deactivate a virtual environment

```none
deactivate
```

See more here: _[Install packages in a virtual environment using pip and venv](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/installing-using-pip-and-virtual-environments/)_

**virtualenv** is the tool of choice for Python 2, while **venv** handles the task in Python 3.

Yet, you can create the virtual environment for Python 3 using any of them.

### Using `venv`

```none
python3 -m venv virtualenvname
```

Command syntax:

```none
/path/to/python3 -m venv /path/to/directory/virtual_env_name
```

### Using `virtualenv`

```none
virtualenv -p python3 virtualenvname
```

Command Syntax:

```none
virtualenv -p /path/to/python3 /path/to/directory/virtual_env_name
```

### Activate the virtual environment

On Linux, Unix or macOS, using the terminal or Bash shell:

```none
source /path/to/venv/bin/activate
```

E.g., `source virtualenvname/bin/activate`

On Unix or macOS, using the [C shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_shell) shell (executable `csh`):

```none
source /path/to/venv/bin/activate.csh
```

On Unix or macOS, using the [Fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_(Unix_shell)) shell:

```none
source /path/to/venv/bin/activate.fish
```

On Windows using the [Command Prompt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cmd.exe):

```none
path\to\venv\Scripts\activate.bat
```

On Windows using [PowerShell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerShell):

```none
path\to\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

### Deactivating the virtual environment

On Linux, Unix or macOS, using the terminal or Bash shell:

```none
deactivate
```

On Windows using the Command Prompt:

```none
path\to\venv\Scripts\deactivate.bat
```

On Windows using PowerShell:

```none
deactivate
```

This answer is for those who may use a different operating system.

Python already ships with its built-in "virtualenv" called `venv` since version 3.3. You no longer need to install or download the `virtualenv` scripts for Python 3.3 and later.

See _[venv — Creation of virtual environments](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html)_.

Check that your installation provided the `pyvenv` command that should take care of creating the "virtualenv". Arguments are similar to the classic virtualenv project.

```none
pyvenv --help
```

Output:

```none
usage: venv [-h] [--system-site-packages] [--symlinks | --copies] [--clear]
            [--upgrade] [--without-pip]
            ENV_DIR [ENV_DIR ...]

Creates virtual Python environments in one or more target directories.

positional arguments:
  ENV_DIR               A directory to create the environment in.

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --system-site-packages
                        Give the virtual environment access to the system
                        site-packages dir.
  --symlinks            Try to use symlinks rather than copies, when symlinks
                        are not the default for the platform.
  --copies              Try to use copies rather than symlinks, even when
                        symlinks are the default for the platform.
  --clear               Delete the contents of the environment directory if it
                        already exists, before environment creation.
  --upgrade             Upgrade the environment directory to use this version
                        of Python, assuming Python has been upgraded in-place.
  --without-pip         Skips installing or upgrading pip in the virtual
                        environment (pip is bootstrapped by default)

Once an environment has been created, you may wish to activate it, e.g. by
sourcing an activate script in its bin directory.
```

**Create a virtual environment:**

For Python 3 version:

**Command:**`python3 -m venv [environment_name]`

**Example:**`python3 -m venv my_virtual_environment`

For Python 2 version:

**Command:**`python -m [environment_name]`

**Example:**`python -m venv my_virtual_environment`

**Activate a virtual environment in Linux:**

Go to the virtual environment directory, and then open the terminal.

**Command:**`source [environment_name]/bin/activate`

**Example:**`source my_virtual_environment/bin/activate`

**Activate a virtual environment in Windows:**

Go to the virtual environment directory, and then open [cmd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cmd.exe).

**Command:**`[environment_name]\Scripts\activate`

**Example:**`my_virtual_environment\Scripts\activate`

If you are on Windows.

1. Manually download and install the version of Python you want from the [official site](https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/)

2. after installation, search "python" to locate the folder, so you can identify the path

4. Inside the folder of which you want to create the environment, start Bash or Visual Studio Code terminal, or whatever command prompt, type **\[python .exe path\] -m venv \[env name\]** like this:


```none
C:/Users/Path/Programs/Python/Python38/python.exe -m venv myenv
```

5. (Note that you have to change forward slash to backward slash for the path on step 4)

6. Activate the environment like so:


```none
source myenv/Scripts/activate
```

# How to Create a Python Virtual Environment

You’ll create a Python virtual environment and use it to install project dependencies without affecting other projects.

## What you’ll build or solve

You’ll create a virtual environment folder, commonly named `.venv`, activate it, and install packages inside it. Done looks like your terminal uses the venv’s Python instead of your system Python.

## Learn Python on Mimo

[CAREER PATHPython Developer\\
\\
Become a Python developer. Master Python from basics to advanced topics, including data structures, functions, classes, and error handling\\
\\
Beginner friendly](https://mimo.org/courses/python-development) [COURSEPython\\
\\
Start your coding journey with Python. Learn basics, data types, control flow, and more\\
\\
Beginner friendly](https://mimo.org/courses/learn-python)

## When this approach works best

This approach works best when you:

- Work on more than one Python project and each needs different package versions.
- Follow a tutorial that requires installing packages and you don’t want to pollute your system Python.
- Run scripts in a team where everyone should use the same dependency set.

Skip virtual environments when:

- You run Python only inside containers and never install packages directly on your machine.

## Prerequisites

- Python installed
- A terminal
- Basic terminal familiarity

* * *

## Step-by-step instructions

### 1) Go to your project folder

Create a folder for your project or use an existing one, then move into it.

**macOS/Linux:**

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
mkdir my_project
cd my_project
```

**Windows:**

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
mkdirmy_project
cdmy_project
```

### What to look for

If you’re not sure where you are, run:

- macOS/Linux:

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
pwd
```

- Windows (PowerShell):

SQL

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
Get-Location
```

* * *

### 2) Create the virtual environment

Create a venv named `.venv` in the current folder.

**macOS/Linux:**

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
python3-m venv .venv
```

**Windows:**

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
py-mvenv .venv
```

This creates a folder named `.venv/` with its own Python interpreter and `pip`.

### What to look for

If you see `No module named venv`, your Python install is missing venv support. See Troubleshooting.

* * *

### 3) Activate the virtual environment

Activation updates your terminal session so `python` and `pip` point to the venv.

**macOS/Linux:**

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
source .venv/bin/activate
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

### What to look for

- Your prompt often shows `(.venv)` after activation.
- If activation fails in PowerShell, you may need to adjust the execution policy. See Troubleshooting.

* * *

### 4) Confirm the venv interpreter is active

Verify that `python` points to the environment you just created.

**macOS/Linux:**

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
which python
python--version
```

**Windows:**

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
python-c"import sys; print(sys.executable)"
python--version
```

### What to look for

- On macOS/Linux, the path from `which python` should include `.venv`.
- On Windows, `sys.executable` should include `\.venv\`.

* * *

### 5) Install packages in the venv, then deactivate when done

Use `python -m pip` so `pip` matches the active interpreter.

Install one package:

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
python-m pip install requests
```

Install from a `requirements.txt` file:

CSS

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
python-m pip install-r requirements.txt
```

When you’re finished working in that project:

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
deactivate
```

### What to look for

- If `pip` installs succeed but imports fail, the venv may not be active in your current terminal window.
- After `deactivate`, your prompt usually loses the `(.venv)` marker.

* * *

## Examples you can copy

### Example 1: Create and activate a venv, then install one package

**macOS/Linux:**

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
python3-m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python-m pip install requests
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
py-mvenv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python-mpipinstallrequests
```

* * *

### Example 2: Install dependencies for a project using requirements.txt

Create `requirements.txt`:

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
requests
```

Install:

CSS

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
python-m pip install-r requirements.txt
```

Then verify in Python:

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
importrequests
print(requests.__version__)
```

* * *

### Example 3: Run a script inside the venv

Create `main.py`:

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
importrequests

resp=requests.get("https://example.com",timeout=5)
print(resp.status_code)
```

Run:

CSS

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
python main.py
```

* * *

## Common mistakes and how to fix them

### Mistake 1: Installing packages without activating the venv

**What you might do**

Run `pip install ...` from a terminal where the venv is not active.

**Why it breaks**

Packages install into a different Python, so your project can’t import them.

**Fix**

Activate the venv, then install with the interpreter you’ll run:

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
source .venv/bin/activate
python-m pip install requests
```

On Windows:

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python-mpipinstallrequests
```

* * *

### Mistake 2: Creating the venv with one Python, then running with another

**What you might do**

Create a venv, then run `python3 main.py` and get version or import issues.

**Why it breaks**

You bypassed the venv by calling a different interpreter directly.

**Fix**

Activate the venv and run `python`:

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
source .venv/bin/activate
python main.py
```

* * *

## Troubleshooting

### If you see: `No module named venv`

On Ubuntu or Debian, install venv support:

Bash

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code

```
sudo apt install python3-venv
```

Then recreate the virtual environment.

* * *

### If you see (PowerShell): running scripts is disabled on this system

Allow scripts for your user, then retry:

JavaScript

[Open in Mimo](https://app.adjust.com/1bbdlllf) [Open in Mimo](https://mimo.org/web/register) Copy Code


### If pip installs succeed but imports still fail

## Quick recap

- Create a venv: `python3 -m venv .venv` or `py -m venv .venv`.
- Activate it: `source .venv/bin/activate` or `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`.
- Confirm `python` points to `.venv`.
- Install packages with `python -m pip install ...`.
- Deactivate with `deactivate` when you’re done.
